claims.text: The coatings are as-deposited, unstressed multilayers comprising alternating layers of different high-entropy alloys.
Stable coherent interfaces form between the layers.
Coherent interfaces govern resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation.
Suppression of dislocation glide and grain-boundary sliding reduces the overall deformation rate.
The proposed test uses in situ transmission electron microscopy and nanoindentation creep testing.
Testing is proposed at 500 MPa and 500 °C for 100 hours.
A coherent-interface multilayer is expected to exhibit a 30% lower steady-state creep rate than a single-layer high-entropy-alloy coating.
The proposed applicability range is a layer thickness of 100 nm to 1 μm.
The proposed applicability range is an operating temperature of 400–600 °C.
The controlled comparison should contrast multilayer coatings with and without coherent interfaces.
Creep rate and microstructural evolution are the proposed response variables.
The hypothesis is falsified if the coherent-interface multilayer does not have a creep rate at least 20% lower than that of a single-layer coating.

contradictions.description: The experiment design specifies a comparison between multilayers with and without coherent interfaces, but the falsification rule and baseline instead compare a coherent-interface multilayer with a single-layer coating. These are different controls and do not isolate the same variable.

The predicted reduction is 30%, whereas falsification requires a reduction below 20%; outcomes from 20% to less than 30% would fail the quantitative prediction but would not falsify the hypothesis under the stated rule.
